leads.summary: A newly created lock clone can report locked=true from another instance's global secure state, so disabling it retains a nonowner and leaves duplicate lock IPC handlers
leads.consequence: Enable a cloned built-in lock while the original has secured the session: setEnabled disables the original and _syncServices creates the clone before checking old services. Both originals copy the same locked expression. Quickshell v0.3.1 computes WlSessionLock.secure using a process-wide session manager, not the particular WlSessionLock's own held lock; the new clone therefore reads locked=true even when its own sessionLock.locked=false. Disabling the clone while the original still holds the lock retains the nonowner too. Both declare IPC target 'lock', and Quickshell routes only the first registered handler, so configuration and IPC disagree about which lock is active. After the original unlocks, _syncServices has no unlock subscription to promptly remove either disabled instance; if the clone retains a cached locked binding, it can remain the active IPC target after a later rescan. The exact stale-binding duration needs a compositor test, but the nonowner/duplicate-handler case follows from the cited source.
leads.triage: behavioural; sent to Opus as neutral follow-up-1; confirmed and extended (retained instance owns no lock via lockRequested, later re-locks); published as main finding

leads.summary: A valid third-party session-lock service that omits a public locked property still loses ext-session-lock when disabled during a lock
leads.consequence: The manifest and service interface require an Item with a service entry point, not a locked property. A custom third-party keepLoaded service can own a WlSessionLock privately without forwarding its state as instance.locked. When a short shell.json defaults window marks it disabled, or when explicitly disabled, the new predicate returns false and _syncServices destroys it even though it holds the compositor lock. This is a conditional supported plugin shape, not a claim about the specific clone reported in issue #11389: omarchy-plugin-clone copies the built-in Service.qml, which does expose locked. A small custom fixture with WlSessionLock held and no root.locked, under a disposable compositor, would confirm the visible compositor result.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N2 docs, model S8); published as documentation note

leads.summary: The changed auth-path tests pass with the new disabled authentication retention guard made a no-op
leads.consequence: On a disposable copy, changing the authentication guard to `if (shouldRetainDisabledKeepLoaded(authenticationId, AuthServiceStore.get(authenticationId)) && false) continue` still passes both changed headless suites under LC_ALL=C. This plausibly regresses issue #11389 for authentication services while preserving all regex tokens. The runtime smoke's acme.keep-service fixture is not classified as authentication, and its synthetic locked bool is not a WlSessionLock, so its new checks would not catch this mutant either even with a compositor. Add an extracted production _syncServices fixture with a stamped authentication clone in AuthServiceStore and assert identity across locked disable/defaults-window and destruction on unlocked disable; assert get() resolves that same live instance.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (N1 mutants); Sol auth-guard && false mutant corroborates; published as optional test improvement

leads.summary: Open PR #12260 adds an incompatible AuthServiceStore.get() at the same insertion point; simply keeping this PR's getter breaks that PR's test
leads.consequence: The two heads diverge at the exact merge-base d3cfd53b. This PR's get() returns undefined after destroy, whereas #12260 defines get() returning null and adds an assertion for === null after destroy. A 3-way merge of their actual files reports a conflict at get() (not a stacked dependency); an automatic or manual resolution that keeps this PR's implementation makes #12260's authentication-store test fail. Resolve to one getter whose absent return value is null and keep this PR's shouldRetainDisabledKeepLoaded falsy fallback. This is a merge integration hazard, not a current-head failing test; GitHub reports #12260 MERGEABLE against its base, not necessarily against this PR.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #12260 patch via gh api (get returns || null, asserts === null); published as related PR note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up at `58f2abb4`, after the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12937#issuecomment-5787367279) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12937#issuecomment-5841826762).

**Resolved:** explicit disable and clone replacement again tear down an unlocked `keepLoaded` service. [`shouldRetainDisabledKeepLoaded()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/58f2abb4c9e76ee88d80350717eeecea90e7759c/shell/shell.qml#L1025-L1032) now keeps a disabled service only while its instance reports `locked === true`. Among shipped services, only `omarchy.lock` and its clones expose `locked`.

**Verified** in a simulation that runs the extracted reconciliation functions of each revision, with component creation and Quickshell's IPC registry stubbed:

| Operation on a running service | Base | Previous head `2d7bdee5` | This head |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disable `omarchy.idle` | destroyed | retained | destroyed |
| Enable a clone of `omarchy.lock` (unlocked) | original destroyed, clone serves `lock` IPC | original retained, keeps `lock` IPC | original destroyed, clone serves `lock` IPC |
| #11389 defaults window with a locked lock clone | clone destroyed and recreated | same instance kept | same instance kept |

This verifies the reconciliation decisions, not native `ext-session-lock` recovery.

## A disabled lock can be kept without owning the session lock

The author's claim holds while unlocked. While the screen is locked, `locked` means "requested or held" (`lockRequested || sessionLock.locked || sessionLock.secure`, [`lock/Service.qml:46`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/58f2abb4c9e76ee88d80350717eeecea90e7759c/shell/plugins/lock/Service.qml#L46)), and a new lock instance can raise `lockRequested` without ever holding a lock. A source trace (Omarchy and Quickshell v0.3.1) of enabling and then disabling a lock clone while another lock instance holds the session:

```text
new lock instance created while another instance holds the lock
  -> checkStrandedLock(): omarchy-hyprland-session-locked exits 0 for any held lock
  -> treats the other instance's lock as stranded, beginLock(): lockRequested = true
  -> requestSessionLock() returns early (global sessionLock.secure), timer keeps retrying
instance disabled
  -> locked === true, so shouldRetainDisabledKeepLoaded() keeps it (owns no lock)
holder unlocks
  -> retained, disabled instance's pending timer takes a new session lock
```

The retention step is model-verified. The stranded-check and re-lock steps are source-traced only. The issue #11389 journal shows the same `lock-stranded: recovering -> lock-requested` sequence at base, most likely from the built-in lock the defaults window created.

**Impact:** after unlocking, a second lock screen can come from a plugin the registry reports disabled, while `lock` IPC and `lock status` still answer from the original holder. Separately, nothing re-runs `_syncServices()` on unlock (its only callers are startup, `pluginsChanged` and rescan), so a retained instance is torn down only at the first config change or rescan after its `locked` turns false, not at unlock. The trigger is uncommon: a clone enable and disable issued while locked (from a TTY, SSH or a script), or, not reproduced, the #11389 defaults window itself, if it lasts long enough for the built-in lock it creates to start a request and closes before unlock. It is still an improvement over base, which destroys the holder in the same sequence and strands the session. This was not reproduced in a live compositor.

**Suggested change:** in the stranded-lock check, ignore a lock already held by another instance in the same shell (for example, re-read `sessionLock.secure` in the helper's exit handler before recovering), so no spurious request is raised. Re-running reconciliation when a retained instance's `locked` becomes false would end retention at unlock. Otherwise, the comment at `shell.qml:981-986` could say that retention also covers pending requests and lasts until the next reconciliation.

**Optional test improvement:** the #11389 path (a lock clone, reconciled through `AuthServiceStore`) is covered only by source-text checks. With the auth-path call passing `null` instead of `AuthServiceStore.get(...)`, or the predicate made to ignore `locked` or never retain, `plugins-test.sh` and the headless part of `plugin-auth-boundary-test.sh` still pass. The runtime smoke fixture is a non-clone service on the `_services` path, so it would not catch the auth-path mutations either. A Node `vm` test that runs `_syncServices` with a locked lock-clone entry in `AuthServiceStore`, checking retention while locked and teardown while unlocked, would cover the fix.

**Documentation:** [`docs/omarchy-shell.md`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/58f2abb4c9e76ee88d80350717eeecea90e7759c/docs/omarchy-shell.md) describes `keepLoaded` as surviving between summons and across hot-reload, but not disable. Retention across disable now depends on the root object exposing `locked`, so a hand-written third-party lock without that property is torn down in the defaults window, as at base.

**Related PR:** #12260 adds `AuthServiceStore.get()` at the same place, returning `null` for a missing id and asserting `get(...) === null` after destroy. This PR's getter returns `undefined`. The two changes will conflict. Keeping #12260's `null`-returning getter would satisfy both, since this PR's call site treats `null` the same way.

**Test scope:** Pinned source review of this head, the previous head and the merge-base; Quickshell v0.3.1 source; an extracted-code reconciliation simulation with stubbed component creation and IPC registry; repository `plugins-test.sh` and `plugin-auth-boundary-test.sh` at each revision plus labelled mutants, run in a sandbox. The runtime smoke test and auth-boundary runtime parts skipped (no compositor). No live Quickshell/Wayland lock, authentication, fingerprint or suspend/resume test was run.
